current_law_statement: Researched 2026-08-19 against the codified Illinois Freedom of Information Act, 5 ILCS 140 (full-Act text opened on ilga.gov, plus per-section pages). Sessions reviewed: 103rd and 104th General Assemblies (2024-2026 Public Acts). The fee section, 5 ILCS 140/6, was last amended by P.A. 98-1129 (eff. 12-3-14) — no 2024-2026 amendment touches Sec. 6, 3.1, 3.2 or 3.6. P.A. 104-438 (eff. 1-1-26) amended Secs. 2, 3 and 4 (definition of 'person'/'junk mail', electronic-request body requirement, person-verification tolling, website posting) without changing the fee-forfeiture clauses in 3(d)/(f) or the fee-posting duty in 4(b); P.A. 104-300 (eff. 1-1-27) and 104-443/104-438 (eff. 1-1-26) touch Sec. 7/7.5 exemptions only. Codified statutes fully available. Guidance reviewed: AG Public Access Counselor FOIA FAQ (10/2023), 'FOIA for Public Bodies' webinar (4/10/2025), PAC Update Winter 2026, and PAC binding opinion 25-014 (Dec. 3, 2025). Guidance restates the statute; the one gap is the FAQ describing the Sec. 6(c) waiver as discretionary where the statute reads 'shall ... as determined by the public body'. Illinois has no AG or agency rule setting FOIA fee amounts; the statute delegates the operative scale to each public body (Sec. 6(b), 4(b)) within fixed ceilings, so municipal and State-agency regimes are the same regime.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (black-and-white, letter or legal size, pages beyond the first 50)
resolutions.source_language: The fee for black and white, letter or legal sized copies shall not exceed 15 cents per page. No fees shall be charged for the first 50 pages of black and white, letter or legal sized copies requested by a requester.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: 'Public body' (5 ILCS 140/2(a)) expressly includes cities, villages and incorporated towns, so the 15-cent ceiling binds municipalities directly. The city sets its operative rate at or below the ceiling in the 'standard scale of fees, established and made public' (IL-9002) and must post 'any fees allowable under Section 6' (Sec. 4(b)). Outer bound remains actual cost of reproduction (IL-9001). Per PAC binding opinion 25-015 (Dec. 23, 2025, summarized in PAC Update Winter 2026) the 15-cent fee is available only when the records are maintained in paper format; records maintained electronically are limited to the recording-medium cost (IL-0031, IL-9013).

resolutions.unit: actual cost for reproducing the records
resolutions.source_language: If a public body provides copies in color or in a size other than letter or legal, the public body may not charge more than its actual cost for reproducing the records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: No numeric color rate; the statute caps color copies at the public body's actual reproduction cost, and Sec. 6(b) bars folding search/review or other personnel costs into that actual cost (Q: 'In calculating its actual cost...'). Prior snippet's 15 cents belongs to B&W only, not color.

resolutions.unit: actual cost for reproducing the records
resolutions.source_language: If a public body provides copies in color or in a size other than letter or legal, the public body may not charge more than its actual cost for reproducing the records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: 'a size other than letter or legal' = oversized/nonstandard. Actual-cost ceiling, no number.

resolutions.unit: fees reasonably calculated to reimburse actual cost of reproducing (photos, maps, transcripts and other non-standard media); except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute
resolutions.source_language: Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute, each public body may charge fees reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost for reproducing and certifying public records and for the use, by any person, of the equipment of the public body to copy records. If a public body provides copies in color or in a size other than letter or legal, the public body may not charge more than its actual cost for reproducing the records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: FOIA sets no specialty schedule; the general 6(b) actual-cost reimbursement standard governs paper/photographic reproductions, and 6(a) limits electronically maintained records (photos, audio, video, GIS data) to the recording medium. The prior values ($20/$40/$100) are the Sec. 6(a-5) voluminous electronic-data tiers (IL-0038), NOT a specialty rate. Statutory carve-out 'Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute' — for municipalities the operative example is traffic crash reports, 625 ILCS 5/11-416: local law enforcement may charge not to exceed $5 per copy ($20 for crash-reconstruction reports) (IL-9010; the AG PAC webinar 4/10/2025 cites this example). Sec. 6(e) delegates driver's-record abstracts to 625 ILCS 5/6-118 ($20; Secretary of State only, IL-9012).

resolutions.unit: USD per page, black-and-white letter/legal copies, per requester
resolutions.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 50 pages of black and white, letter or legal sized copies requested by a requester. The fee for black and white, letter or legal sized copies shall not exceed 15 cents per page.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: The state prescribes exactly two bands: first 50 B&W letter/legal pages free (fixed, city cannot charge), thereafter a single ceiling of 15 cents. No volume-graduated bands beyond that; a city may set lower rates or its own sub-15-cent gradations in its published standard scale (IL-9002). Prior values '8 hours' belong to commercial labor (IL-0036), not page tiers.

resolutions.unit: pages (black-and-white, letter or legal size) 'requested by a requester'
resolutions.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 50 pages of black and white, letter or legal sized copies requested by a requester.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.manual_verification: Statute says 'first 50 pages ... requested by a requester' without stating a per-request vs per-period unit; the AG FAQ (10/2023) and PAC binding opinion 25-015 apply it per request. Confirm the unit convention with counsel if a city wants a per-period reading.
resolutions.notes: Applies only to B&W letter/legal paper copies; color/oversized and electronic records have no free-page allowance (they are on actual-cost/medium bases). Not waivable downward by the city.

resolutions.source_language: If a request is not a request for a commercial purpose or a voluminous request, a public body may not charge the requester for the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records. In calculating its actual cost for reproducing records or for the use of the equipment of the public body to reproduce records, a public body shall not include the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records, except for commercial requests as provided in subsection (f) of this Section. A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions. The provisions of this subsection (f) apply only to commercial requests.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: For ordinary (non-commercial) municipal requests, search/retrieval labor is categorically non-chargeable, so a search labor rate cannot exist. Sole exception: commercial-purpose requests, ceiling $10 per hour after the first 8 free hours (IL-0035/IL-0036; see item 'commercial'). Ambiguity for manual note: Sec. 6(a) exempts 'voluminous' requests from its personnel-cost prohibition, but Sec. 6(b) still excludes personnel costs from actual reproduction cost 'except for commercial requests', and the only voluminous-specific fee is the 6(a-5) megabyte tiers; the AG FAQ (10/2023) states search/review fees exist only 'in rare circumstances only applicable to commercial requests'.

resolutions.source_authority: 5 ILCS 140/6(a), 6(b), 6(f); Ill. Att'y Gen. Pub. Acc. Op. No. 25-014 (Dec. 3, 2025)
resolutions.source_language: If a request is not a request for a commercial purpose or a voluminous request, a public body may not charge the requester for the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records. In calculating its actual cost for reproducing records or for the use of the equipment of the public body to reproduce records, a public body shall not include the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records, except for commercial requests as provided in subsection (f) of this Section. A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions. The provisions of this subsection (f) apply only to commercial requests.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: Review/redaction labor is non-chargeable for non-commercial requests. PAC binding opinion 25-014 (Mattoon Police Dept., body-camera video) confirms a public body may not recover redaction costs (there, $2.58/minute redaction-software cost) for electronically maintained records; fee limited to recording medium (IL-9011). Commercial-only exception: 'examining the record for necessary redactions' up to $10/hour (IL-0035).

resolutions.source_language: If a request is not a request for a commercial purpose or a voluminous request, a public body may not charge the requester for the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records. Except to the extent that the General Assembly expressly provides, statutory fees applicable to copies of public records when furnished in a paper format shall not be applicable to those records when furnished in an electronic format.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: 'other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records' (which would include programming/data-extraction time) may not be charged on non-commercial, non-voluminous requests, and no hourly programming rate exists anywhere in the Act. Voluminous requests for electronic records are charged, if at all, on the flat 6(a-5) megabyte tiers ($20/$40/$100 ceilings, IL-0038) — the prior values on this item are those tiers, not a programming rate. Sec. 6(a) also requires furnishing electronic records in the requester's specified format 'if feasible' (IL-0034), which the AG reads as not requiring creation of new records.

resolutions.value: never (non-commercial requests) | commercial requests: only above 8 personnel hours, all media
resolutions.source_language: If a request is not a request for a commercial purpose or a voluminous request, a public body may not charge the requester for the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records. A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions. No fees shall be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel in searching for or retrieving a requested record. The provisions of this subsection (f) apply only to commercial requests.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: Labor (search, retrieval, redaction examination) is chargeable ONLY on commercial-purpose requests (5 ILCS 140/2(c-10) definition), and only for hours beyond the first 8, at up to $10/hour. There is no page threshold and no paper-only carve-out. Voluminous requests: no hourly labor; flat 6(a-5) electronic-data tiers only.

resolutions.source_language: In calculating its actual cost for reproducing records or for the use of the equipment of the public body to reproduce records, a public body shall not include the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records, except for commercial requests as provided in subsection (f) of this Section. A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: No overhead/fringe multiplier exists: non-commercial labor is non-chargeable, and the commercial hourly charge is an all-in ceiling of $10 per hour with no add-on authorized. Coverage: Searched 5 ILCS 140 (full Act text on ilga.gov incl. Secs. 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 4, 6, 9.5), 2024-2026 Public Acts touching the Act (P.A. 103-865, 104-300, 104-438, 104-443), the AG Public Access Counselor FOIA FAQ (10/2023), the PAC 'FOIA for Public Bodies' webinar (4/10/2025), the PAC Update Winter 2026 (P.A. 104-438 summary; binding opinions 25-014, 25-015), and PAC binding opinion 25-014. The Attorney General has no fee-setting rule for public bodies (no delegation in Sec. 6 to an administrative instrument except Sec. 6(e), Vehicle Code driver's-record fee).

Only relevant to commercial requests (labor otherwise non-chargeable). Coverage: Searched 5 ILCS 140 (full Act text on ilga.gov incl. Secs. 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 4, 6, 9.5), 2024-2026 Public Acts touching the Act (P.A. 103-865, 104-300, 104-438, 104-443), the AG Public Access Counselor FOIA FAQ (10/2023), the PAC 'FOIA for Public Bodies' webinar (4/10/2025), the PAC Update Winter 2026 (P.A. 104-438 summary; binding opinions 25-014, 25-015), and PAC binding opinion 25-014. resolutions.unit: hours of personnel search/retrieval time per commercial request (non-commercial requests: all labor free, no cap)
resolutions.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel in searching for or retrieving a requested record. The provisions of this subsection (f) apply only to commercial requests.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: The 8 free hours attach to commercial requests only (Sec. 6(f) 'apply only to commercial requests'). For every other request the correct engine value is 'unlimited' because search/review labor is categorically non-chargeable (IL-0032). Note the free-hours clause names 'searching for or retrieving' — it does not literally name redaction examination; treat with counsel.

resolutions.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel in searching for or retrieving a requested record.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: No Texas-style per-requester monthly/annual free-time allowance. The recurrent-requester regime (2(g): 50 requests/12 months, 15/30 days, 7/7 days) changes response timing (21 business days, IL-0020) and permits full prepayment (IL-0019), not free-hour accounting. Coverage: Searched 5 ILCS 140 (full Act text on ilga.gov incl. Secs. 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 4, 6, 9.5), 2024-2026 Public Acts touching the Act (P.A. 103-865, 104-300, 104-438, 104-443), the AG Public Access Counselor FOIA FAQ (10/2023), the PAC 'FOIA for Public Bodies' webinar (4/10/2025), the PAC Update Winter 2026 (P.A. 104-438 summary; binding opinions 25-014, 25-015), and PAC binding opinion 25-014. resolutions.value: no dollar/hour threshold; a fee estimate is a mandatory element of the response for commercial-purpose (Sec. 3.1(a)), recurrent-requester (Sec. 3.2(a)) and voluminous (Sec. 3.6(c)) requests; no estimate duty for ordinary requests
resolutions.source_language: The response shall (i) provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents, (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act, (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions, or (iv) provide the records requested.
resolutions.notes: Illinois gates the estimate by request CLASS, not by amount. Shape for the engine: on classifying a request as commercial / recurrent / voluminous, the response option (i) is 'an estimate of the time required ... and an estimate of the fees to be charged'. Related: Sec. 6(f)/(a-5) accounting duty after fees are imposed (IL-0037), and Sec. 6(d) — a fee inconsistent with 6(a)/(b) is a denial (IL-9004).

resolutions.source_language: The response shall: (i) provide an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents; (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act; (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions; or (iv) provide the records requested.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: No provision that a requester must accept/respond to a fee estimate within N days or the request is withdrawn. Do not confuse with the voluminous 10-business-day window to AMEND the request after the Sec. 3.6(a) notice (IL-0025), which precedes the estimate. resolutions.source_language: If a public body imposes a fee pursuant to this subsection (f), it must provide the requester with an accounting of all fees, costs, and personnel hours in connection with the request for public records.

resolutions.manual_verification: Whether a public body may condition an ORDINARY request's copies on prior payment is not addressed in the Act or in the AG FAQ/webinar reviewed; treat as a city-policy question pending PAC guidance.
resolutions.notes: Illinois has a class gate, not an amount gate. Sec. 3(b) makes the duty to provide copies 'Subject to the fee provisions of Section 6', but Sec. 6 contains no prepayment clause for ordinary requests.

resolutions.unit: % of the estimated fee (commercial-purpose, recurrent-requester and voluminous requests only)

resolutions.manual_verification: The statute authorizes requiring payment 'in full before copying'; reading that as a 100% ceiling on a pre-copy deposit is a scope judgment (the Act never uses the word 'deposit'). Silent for ordinary requests.
resolutions.notes: Permission, not requirement: the public body 'may require the person to pay in full before copying'. A city may take less than the full estimate. Not applicable to ordinary requests (see rules.deposit.threshold).

resolutions.value: pay_in_full_before_copying (commercial-purpose, recurrent-requester, voluminous requests); silent for ordinary requests
resolutions.source_language: The response shall: (i) provide an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents; (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act; (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions; or (iv) provide the records requested. If a requester does not pay a fee charged pursuant to Section 6 of this Act for a voluminous request, the debt shall be considered a debt due and owing to the public body and may be collected in accordance with applicable law. This fee may be charged by the public body even if the requester fails to accept or collect records the public body has prepared in response to a voluminous request.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Secs. 3.1, 3.2, 3.6 unamended 2024-2026)
resolutions.notes: The gate is 'before copying' (i.e., before reproduction begins), not merely before release. For voluminous requests the fee is owed even if the requester never collects the records (IL-9005). Sec. 3(d)/(f) forfeits any copy fee when the public body missed its deadline (IL-9008), which the engine should check before applying any gate.

resolutions.value: voluminous requests: unpaid Sec. 6 fee is 'a debt due and owing to the public body' collectible under applicable law, chargeable even if records are not accepted/collected; no withdrawal-after-N-days rule; no prior-debt prepayment rule; silent for other request classes

resolutions.notes: No overrun/re-issue rule (no revised-estimate requirement, no bar on collecting above the estimate, no clock restart). The 6(f)/(a-5) accounting (IL-0037) is a post-hoc itemization, not a re-estimate. Coverage: Searched 5 ILCS 140 (full Act text on ilga.gov incl. Secs. 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 4, 6, 9.5), 2024-2026 Public Acts touching the Act (P.A. 103-865, 104-300, 104-438, 104-443), the AG Public Access Counselor FOIA FAQ (10/2023), the PAC 'FOIA for Public Bodies' webinar (4/10/2025), the PAC Update Winter 2026 (P.A. 104-438 summary; binding opinions 25-014, 25-015), and PAC binding opinion 25-014. The Attorney General has no fee-setting rule for public bodies (no delegation in Sec. 6 to an administrative instrument except Sec. 6(e), Vehicle Code driver's-record fee).

resolutions.value: credit/debit/electronic card acceptance is authorized but not required for units of local government (governing-body election after public hearing, 50 ILCS 345/20(a)); convenience fee/surcharge permitted only up to the processing cost actually incurred (345/25(a)) and may not be retained in excess of that cost (345/15(e)); FOIA itself is silent
resolutions.source_language: (a) Any unit of local government and any community college district that has the authority to accept the payment of funds for any purpose is authorized, but not required, to accept payment by credit card. (a) The governing body of a local governmental entity authorizing acceptance of payment by credit card may, but is not required to, impose a convenience fee or surcharge upon a cardholder making payment by credit card in an amount to wholly or partially offset, but in no event exceed, the amount of any discount or processing fee incurred by the local governmental entity.
resolutions.manual_verification: The Local Governmental Acceptance of Credit Cards Act is a general-purpose statute for 'any fine, fee, charge, tax, or cost' of a unit of local government — it is not FOIA-specific and the FOIA Act itself says nothing about payment method. Confirm the city's governing body has made the Sec. 20(a) election before offering card payment for FOIA fees.
resolutions.notes: Applies to units of local government (municipalities included), not to State agencies (which are governed by separate State Treasurer/CMS provisions). Sec. 25(b)-(c) caps card fees for licenses/permits/fines/taxes; a FOIA copy fee is not one of the named categories, so the general 25(a) 'not exceed the processing fee' rule is the operative bound.

resolutions.unit: fees reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost for reproducing and certifying (paper); actual cost of the recording medium (electronic); no dollar maximum
resolutions.source_language: Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute, each public body may charge fees reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost for reproducing and certifying public records and for the use, by any person, of the equipment of the public body to copy records. A public body may charge the requester for the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium. The imposition of a fee not consistent with subsections (6)(a) and (b) of this Act constitutes a denial of access to public records for the purposes of judicial review.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: The request-level cap is the actual-cost standard itself: nothing above actual reproduction/certification cost (paper) or medium cost (electronic) is lawful, and Sec. 6(d) converts an inconsistent fee into a denial reviewable in court (and by the PAC under Sec. 9.5). The only fixed dollar caps are per-band: 15 cents/page (IL-0028), $1 certification (IL-0030), $10/hour commercial labor (IL-0035), $20/$40/$100 voluminous electronic-data tiers per format (IL-0038).

resolutions.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 50 pages of black and white, letter or legal sized copies requested by a requester.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: No dollar de-minimis ('no charge below $X'). The functional equivalents are page-based (first 50 B&W letter/legal pages free, IL-0027) and the discretionary public-interest waiver/reduction (IL-0033). A city may adopt a dollar de-minimis in its standard scale (IL-9002) since fees are permissive ('may charge'). Coverage: Searched 5 ILCS 140 (full Act text on ilga.gov incl. Secs. 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 4, 6, 9.5), 2024-2026 Public Acts touching the Act (P.A. 103-865, 104-300, 104-438, 104-443), the AG Public Access Counselor FOIA FAQ (10/2023), the PAC 'FOIA for Public Bodies' webinar (4/10/2025), the PAC Update Winter 2026 (P.A. 104-438 summary; binding opinions 25-014, 25-015), and PAC binding opinion 25-014. The Attorney General has no fee-setting rule for public bodies (no delegation in Sec. 6 to an administrative instrument except Sec. 6(e), Vehicle Code driver's-record fee).

resolutions.source_language: Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute, each public body may charge fees reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost for reproducing and certifying public records and for the use, by any person, of the equipment of the public body to copy records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: No minimum fee. Any flat minimum would have to fit within 'reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost' (IL-9001) and the 50-free-page rule; the Act does not authorize one expressly. Coverage: Searched 5 ILCS 140 (full Act text on ilga.gov incl. Secs. 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 4, 6, 9.5), 2024-2026 Public Acts touching the Act (P.A. 103-865, 104-300, 104-438, 104-443), the AG Public Access Counselor FOIA FAQ (10/2023), the PAC 'FOIA for Public Bodies' webinar (4/10/2025), the PAC Update Winter 2026 (P.A. 104-438 summary; binding opinions 25-014, 25-015), and PAC binding opinion 25-014. The Attorney General has no fee-setting rule for public bodies (no delegation in Sec. 6 to an administrative instrument except Sec. 6(e), Vehicle Code driver's-record fee).

resolutions.unit: actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium
resolutions.source_authority: 5 ILCS 140/6(a); Ill. Att'y Gen. Pub. Acc. Op. No. 25-014
resolutions.source_language: A public body may charge the requester for the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: Medium purchase cost only — no per-page, staff-time or software cost may be added (PAC 25-014). If delivered by e-mail/portal there is no medium and therefore no charge (see 'delivery'). Voluminous electronic requests: 6(a-5) tiers may be charged instead/in addition (IL-0038; the Act does not say whether medium cost stacks on the tier — manual note).

resolutions.source_language: Except to the extent that the General Assembly expressly provides, statutory fees applicable to copies of public records when furnished in a paper format shall not be applicable to those records when furnished in an electronic format. A public body may charge the actual cost of retrieving and transporting public records from an off-site storage facility when the public records are maintained by a third-party storage company under contract with the public body.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.manual_verification: Postage/mailing/handling: not addressed by the Act, the AG FAQ (10/2023) or the 4/10/2025 PAC webinar; a city charging actual postage should confirm with the PAC. Electronic delivery (e-mail/portal): no charge is authorized beyond the medium (none exists) — high confidence.
resolutions.notes: Electronic delivery: Sec. 6(a) makes paper-copy fees inapplicable to records furnished electronically and limits charges to the recording medium, so e-mailed records carry no fee (IL-9013). Pickup: no charge stated. Off-site retrieval/transport: actual cost, COMMERCIAL requests only, when records are held by a contracted third-party storage company (IL-9007). Coverage: Searched 5 ILCS 140 (full Act text on ilga.gov incl. Secs. 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 4, 6, 9.5), 2024-2026 Public Acts touching the Act (P.A. 103-865, 104-300, 104-438, 104-443), the AG Public Access Counselor FOIA FAQ (10/2023), the PAC 'FOIA for Public Bodies' webinar (4/10/2025), the PAC Update Winter 2026 (P.A. 104-438 summary; binding opinions 25-014, 25-015), and PAC binding opinion 25-014. The Attorney General has no fee-setting rule for public bodies (no delegation in Sec. 6 to an administrative instrument except Sec. 6(e), Vehicle Code driver's-record fee).

resolutions.source_language: The cost for certifying a record shall not exceed $1.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: 'shall not exceed $1' — ceiling; the city sets the operative certification charge at or below $1 in its standard scale. Sec. 3(b) requires certification 'if so requested'. Applies to all public bodies incl. municipalities.

resolutions.unit: actual cost of purchasing the recording medium; no per-recording, per-minute or free-minute figures exist
resolutions.source_authority: 5 ILCS 140/6(a); 6(a-5); Ill. Att'y Gen. Pub. Acc. Op. No. 25-014 (Dec. 3, 2025)
resolutions.source_language: A public body may charge the requester for the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium. 11) Because the Department maintains the requested video footage in electronic format, section 6(a) of FOIA limits the copying fee to the actual cost of the recording medium.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Sec. 6 unamended since P.A. 98-1129; PAC 25-014 issued Dec. 3, 2025, binding on the parties and reviewable under 5 ILCS 140/11.5)
resolutions.notes: Audio/video (incl. body-camera footage under the Law Enforcement Officer-Worn Body Camera Act) are electronically maintained records: only the medium cost may be charged; a per-minute redaction charge ($2.58/min) was held improper in PAC 25-014. The prior values $20/$40/$100 are the 6(a-5) megabyte tiers, which apply only if the request is 'voluminous' (5 ILCS 140/2(h)) — video files can reach those tiers quickly, so the engine should evaluate the voluminous classification, not a per-minute rate.

resolutions.value: surcharge_pct: none | labor: 10.00 USD per personnel hour after the first 8 free hours (search, retrieval, examination for necessary redactions) | off-site third-party storage retrieval/transport: actual cost | accounting of all fees, costs and personnel hours required
resolutions.unit: USD per hour; commercial-purpose requests only (5 ILCS 140/2(c-10))
resolutions.basis: ceiling (labor) / soft-standard actual cost (off-site) / fixed (8 free hours)
resolutions.source_language: A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions. No fees shall be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel in searching for or retrieving a requested record. A public body may charge the actual cost of retrieving and transporting public records from an off-site storage facility when the public records are maintained by a third-party storage company under contract with the public body. If a public body imposes a fee pursuant to this subsection (f), it must provide the requester with an accounting of all fees, costs, and personnel hours in connection with the request for public records. The provisions of this subsection (f) apply only to commercial requests.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.notes: No percentage surcharge exists; the commercial schedule is (a) labor becomes chargeable at up to $10/hour beyond 8 hours, (b) off-site retrieval actual cost, (c) same copy fees as everyone else, (d) full prepayment may be required with the estimate (IL-0019), (e) 21-working-day response window (IL-0017), (f) commercial requesters cannot seek PAC review except of the commercial classification itself (Sec. 9.5(b)). 'Commercial purpose' excludes news media and non-profit/scientific/academic organizations for news, opinion or research purposes.

resolutions.value: grounds: requester states the specific purpose AND indicates waiver/reduction is in the public interest (principal purpose = access and disseminate information on health, safety and welfare or legal rights of the general public, not principally personal/commercial benefit; news media exempt from 'commercial benefit') | mandatory_vs_discretionary: 'shall be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge, as determined by the public body' — the trigger is mandatory, the amount (full vs partial) is discretionary | purpose_statement: required (one of the two purpose inquiries the Act allows, Sec. 3(c)) | written_denial: no waiver-specific written-denial clause | appeal: no waiver-specific appeal; Sec. 6(d) treats fees inconsistent with 6(a)/(b) as denials (waiver is 6(c))
resolutions.source_language: Documents shall be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge, as determined by the public body, if the person requesting the documents states the specific purpose for the request and indicates that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest. Waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest if the principal purpose of the request is to access and disseminate information regarding the health, safety and welfare or the legal rights of the general public and is not for the principal purpose of personal or commercial benefit. For purposes of this subsection, "commercial benefit" shall not apply to requests made by news media when the principal purpose of the request is to access and disseminate information regarding the health, safety, and welfare or the legal rights of the general public. In setting the amount of the waiver or reduction, the public body may take into consideration the amount of materials requested and the cost of copying them.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
resolutions.manual_verification: Whether refusal of a 6(c) waiver is itself a 'denial' reviewable by the PAC under Sec. 9.5 is not settled in the statute (Sec. 6(d) names only 6(a) and (b)); flag for counsel/PAC guidance.
resolutions.notes: The AG FAQ (10/2023) describes the waiver as 'may, but are not required to' — a guidance-vs-statute tension: the statute's operative verb is 'shall' with the public body determining the amount. Statute governs; note the inconsistency. In setting the amount the body 'may take into consideration the amount of materials requested and the cost of copying them'.

resolutions.unit: boolean — copy fee forfeited when the public body misses the Sec. 3 response deadline (or the extended deadline) and later provides the copies
resolutions.source_language: A public body that fails to respond to a request within the requisite periods in this Section but thereafter provides the requester with copies of the requested public records may not impose a fee for such copies. A public body that fails to respond to a request within the time permitted for extension but thereafter provides the requester with copies of the requested public records may not impose a fee for those copies.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/3 last amended by P.A. 104-438, eff. 1-1-26; the quoted clause is unchanged by that Act)
resolutions.notes: Statutory, not discretionary. Per Sec. 3(i) the Sec. 3 time periods (and thus this forfeiture) do not apply to commercial-purpose, recurrent-requester or voluminous requests, which run on Secs. 3.1/3.2/3.6 — the AG FAQ (10/2023) states the same. Also bars treating the late-answered request as unduly burdensome.

resolutions.value: repeat: 'Repeated requests from the same person for the same records that are unchanged or identical to records previously provided or properly denied' are deemed unduly burdensome (may be denied under 3(g)) | aggregation into 'voluminous': >5 individual requests for >5 categories, or a combination totalling >5 categories, within 20 business days; or >500 letter/legal pages (single record excepted) | 'recurrent requester': 50 requests/12 months, 15/30 days, or 7/7 days to the same public body | no fee carry-forward rule
resolutions.source_language: Repeated requests from the same person for the same records that are unchanged or identical to records previously provided or properly denied under this Act shall be deemed unduly burdensome under this provision. "Voluminous request" means a request that: (i) includes more than 5 individual requests for more than 5 different categories of records or a combination of individual requests that total requests for more than 5 different categories of records in a period of 20 business days; or (ii) requires the compilation of more than 500 letter or legal-sized pages of public records unless a single requested record exceeds 500 pages.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/3 last amended by P.A. 104-438, eff. 1-1-26; the quoted clause is unchanged by that Act)
resolutions.notes: Aggregation in Illinois changes the request's CLASS (voluminous → 6(a-5) tiers, prepayment, 3.6 clocks; recurrent → 21-business-day clock, prepayment), not the fee arithmetic per se; there is no carry-forward of unpaid balances or free-page allowances across requests. News media and non-profit/scientific/academic requesters are excluded from the voluminous and recurrent counts.

new_rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost reimbursement standard for reproduction and certification
new_rules.atomic_rule: Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute, a public body may charge fees reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost for reproducing and certifying public records and for the use of its equipment to copy records; that actual cost may not include search, review or other personnel costs except for commercial requests under Sec. 6(f).
new_rules.trigger: Public body charges a fee for reproducing or certifying records
new_rules.source_language: Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute, each public body may charge fees reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost for reproducing and certifying public records and for the use, by any person, of the equipment of the public body to copy records. In calculating its actual cost for reproducing records or for the use of the equipment of the public body to reproduce records, a public body shall not include the costs of any search for and review of the records or other personnel costs associated with reproducing the records, except for commercial requests as provided in subsection (f) of this Section.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Soft-standard outer ceiling ('reasonably calculated to reimburse its actual cost'); the numeric per-band caps (15 cents, $1) sit inside it. 'Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute' preserves record-specific statutory fees (e.g., 625 ILCS 5/11-416 crash reports, IL-9010).

new_rules.legal_concept: Standard scale of fees, established and made public
new_rules.atomic_rule: Fees under Sec. 6(b) must be imposed according to a standard scale of fees established and made public by the public body imposing them, and the public body must prominently display on its website (and post at its offices if it has no website) any fees allowable under Section 6.
new_rules.source_language: Such fees shall be imposed according to a standard scale of fees, established and made public by the body imposing them. (b) A brief description of the methods whereby the public may request information and public records, a directory designating the Freedom of Information officer or officers, the address where requests for public records should be directed, and any fees allowable under Section 6 of this Act.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Sec. 6 P.A. 98-1129 eff. 12-3-14; Sec. 4 last amended P.A. 104-438 eff. 1-1-26 — quoted clause unchanged)
new_rules.notes: The city (governing body) is the fee-setting authority within the state's ceilings; the Act delegates the operative amounts to the public body's published scale. Non-compliant fee = denial (IL-9004).

new_rules.legal_concept: Fee estimate required in commercial / recurrent / voluminous responses
new_rules.atomic_rule: For a commercial-purpose request (21 working days), a recurrent-requester request (21 business days) or a voluminous request (final response under Sec. 3.6(c)), the public body's response, if it does not deny or produce, must provide an estimate of the fees to be charged (and, for commercial and recurrent, of the time required), which it may require the requester to pay in full before copying.
new_rules.trigger: Request classified as commercial-purpose, recurrent-requester or voluminous
new_rules.source_language: The response shall (i) provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents, (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act, (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions, or (iv) provide the records requested. [Sec. 3.6(c):] The response shall: (i) provide an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents; (ii) deny the request pursuant to one or more of the exemptions set out in this Act; (iii) notify the requester that the request is unduly burdensome and extend an opportunity to the requester to attempt to reduce the request to manageable proportions; or (iv) provide the records requested.
new_rules.notes: No dollar/hour threshold anywhere in the Act; the estimate duty is class-based. Ordinary requests carry no estimate duty. Full-prepayment permission is IL-0019.

new_rules.legal_concept: Fee inconsistent with Sec. 6(a)/(b) is a denial
new_rules.atomic_rule: The imposition of a fee not consistent with Sec. 6(a) and (b) constitutes a denial of access to public records for purposes of judicial review.
new_rules.trigger: Public body imposes a fee inconsistent with Sec. 6(a) or 6(b)
new_rules.source_language: The imposition of a fee not consistent with subsections (6)(a) and (b) of this Act constitutes a denial of access to public records for the purposes of judicial review.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Trigger for the appeal path (court under Sec. 11; PAC request for review under Sec. 9.5 — PAC binding opinions 25-014/25-015 reviewed fee assessments as denials). Names only 6(a) and (b), not the 6(c) waiver.

new_rules.legal_concept: Voluminous-request fee is a debt due and owing
new_rules.atomic_rule: If a requester does not pay a Sec. 6 fee charged for a voluminous request, the debt is a debt due and owing to the public body collectible under applicable law, and the fee may be charged even if the requester fails to accept or collect the prepared records; the Sec. 3.6(a) voluminous notice must warn the requester of this.
new_rules.trigger: Voluminous request; fee charged under Sec. 6 unpaid or records not collected
new_rules.source_language: If a requester does not pay a fee charged pursuant to Section 6 of this Act for a voluminous request, the debt shall be considered a debt due and owing to the public body and may be collected in accordance with applicable law. This fee may be charged by the public body even if the requester fails to accept or collect records the public body has prepared in response to a voluminous request.
new_rules.notes: Only nonpayment consequence in the Act; no withdrawal clock, no prior-debt prepayment rule; silent for non-voluminous requests.

new_rules.legal_concept: Local-government credit/debit card acceptance and convenience fee
new_rules.atomic_rule: A unit of local government is authorized, but not required, to accept payment of any fee by credit card (including debit and other electronic cards) upon its governing body's election after a public hearing, and may impose a convenience fee or surcharge on the cardholder that does not exceed the discount or processing fee it incurs; it may not retain any card fee in excess of the amount paid in connection with the transaction.
new_rules.trigger: City elects to accept card payment for FOIA fees
new_rules.source_language: (a) Any unit of local government and any community college district that has the authority to accept the payment of funds for any purpose is authorized, but not required, to accept payment by credit card. (a) The governing body of a local governmental entity authorizing acceptance of payment by credit card may, but is not required to, impose a convenience fee or surcharge upon a cardholder making payment by credit card in an amount to wholly or partially offset, but in no event exceed, the amount of any discount or processing fee incurred by the local governmental entity.
new_rules.notes: General-purpose local-government statute (any 'fine, fee, charge, tax, or cost'), not FOIA-specific; FOIA is silent on payment method. Applies to units of local government (municipalities), not State agencies.

new_rules.legal_concept: Off-site storage retrieval/transport cost (commercial requests only)
new_rules.atomic_rule: On a commercial-purpose request, a public body may charge the actual cost of retrieving and transporting public records from an off-site storage facility when the records are maintained by a third-party storage company under contract with the public body.
new_rules.trigger: Commercial-purpose request; responsive records held off-site by a contracted third-party storage company
new_rules.source_language: A public body may charge the actual cost of retrieving and transporting public records from an off-site storage facility when the public records are maintained by a third-party storage company under contract with the public body. The provisions of this subsection (f) apply only to commercial requests.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: Actual cost, no number. Commercial only. Accounting of all fees/costs/hours required when any 6(f) fee is imposed (IL-0037).

new_rules.atomic_rule: A public body that fails to respond to a request within the Sec. 3 response period (or within the time permitted for an extension) but thereafter provides copies may not impose a fee for those copies, and may not treat the request as unduly burdensome.
new_rules.trigger: Public body misses the Sec. 3(d) 5-business-day deadline or the Sec. 3(e)/(f) extended deadline and later provides copies
new_rules.source_language: A public body that fails to respond to a request within the requisite periods in this Section but thereafter provides the requester with copies of the requested public records may not impose a fee for such copies. A public body that fails to respond to a request within the time permitted for extension but thereafter provides the requester with copies of the requested public records may not impose a fee for those copies.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/3 last amended by P.A. 104-438, eff. 1-1-26; the quoted clause is unchanged by that Act)
new_rules.notes: Sec. 3(i) removes commercial, recurrent and voluminous requests from the Sec. 3 time periods, so the forfeiture does not reach them (AG FAQ 10/2023 agrees). Fixed statutory consequence; the city cannot charge around it.

new_rules.legal_concept: Repeated identical requests deemed unduly burdensome
new_rules.atomic_rule: Repeated requests from the same person for the same records that are unchanged or identical to records previously provided or properly denied are deemed unduly burdensome under Sec. 3(g), permitting denial after the conferral step.
new_rules.trigger: Same requester re-requests records previously provided or properly denied, unchanged
new_rules.source_language: Repeated requests from the same person for the same records that are unchanged or identical to records previously provided or properly denied under this Act shall be deemed unduly burdensome under this provision.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/3 last amended by P.A. 104-438, eff. 1-1-26; the quoted clause is unchanged by that Act)
new_rules.notes: Structural repeat-request rule; no fee carry-forward. Aggregation into 'voluminous' (2(h), >5 categories/20 business days or >500 pages) and 'recurrent requester' (2(g)) are classification rules already in IL-0022/IL-0023.

new_rules.legal_concept: Traffic crash report copy fee (local law enforcement)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency of a local authority may furnish copies of traffic crash reports it prepared and may receive a fee not to exceed $5 per copy, or not to exceed $20 for a crash investigated by a crash reconstruction officer or team.
new_rules.trigger: Request for a copy of a traffic crash report prepared by the municipal police
new_rules.source_language: Other State law enforcement agencies or law enforcement agencies of local authorities may furnish copies of traffic crash reports prepared by such agencies and may receive a fee not to exceed $5 for each copy or in the case of a crash which was investigated by a crash reconstruction officer or crash reconstruction team, the State or local law enforcement agency may receive a fee not to exceed $20.
new_rules.notes: A 'fee otherwise fixed by statute' under 5 ILCS 140/6(b); the AG PAC webinar (4/10/2025) cites it as the example of a statutory fee chargeable instead of the Sec. 6(b) fee. Ceiling; city sets ≤ $5 / ≤ $20. Applies to municipal police (local authorities) as well as State agencies.

new_rules.legal_concept: Electronic records: fee limited to recording medium; no redaction-cost recovery (PAC binding opinion 25-014)
new_rules.atomic_rule: For records maintained in electronic format (there, police body-camera video), Sec. 6(a) limits the copying fee to the actual cost of the recording medium; a public body may not charge to recover the cost of redaction software or per-minute redaction work, and Sec. 6(b)'s actual-cost clause for color/nonstandard paper copies does not apply to video.
new_rules.trigger: Requester seeks copies of electronically maintained records requiring redaction
new_rules.source_language: 11) Because the Department maintains the requested video footage in electronic format, section 6(a) of FOIA limits the copying fee to the actual cost of the recording medium. [Reasoning:] If the General Assembly had intended to allow a public body to charge fees to reimburse the actual cost it incurred to make redactions to copies of records in electronic format, it would have expressly authorized such a fee in section 6(a) of FOIA.
new_rules.source_authority: Ill. Att'y Gen. Pub. Acc. Op. No. 25-014 (Dec. 3, 2025), citing Sage Information Services v. Humm, 2012 IL App (5th) 110580, ¶18 and Sage Information Services v. Suhr, 2014 IL App (2d) 130708, ¶¶14-15
new_rules.effective_status: Current (binding opinion issued Dec. 3, 2025; final administrative decision reviewable under 5 ILCS 140/11.5)
new_rules.notes: Binding on the parties; the PAC applies it generally. Cited appellate holdings: 'the current version of section 6 of the FOIA does not allow a fee in excess of the cost of the electronic medium for the reproduction of electronic records' (Humm) and a non-FOIA statute's fee applies to electronic records only if it expressly says so (Suhr).

new_rules.legal_concept: Driver's-record abstract fee delegated to Vehicle Code (Secretary of State)
new_rules.atomic_rule: The fee for each abstract of a driver's record is as provided in 625 ILCS 5/6-118, whether furnished on paper or electronically; 6-118(a-5) fixes the fee for a driver's record or data contained therein at $20.
new_rules.trigger: Request for an abstract of a driver's record
new_rules.source_language: The fee for each abstract of a driver's record shall be as provided in Section 6-118 of "The Illinois Vehicle Code", approved September 29, 1969, as amended, whether furnished as a paper copy or as an electronic copy. [625 ILCS 5/6-118:] (a-5) The fee for a driver's record or data contained therein is $20 and shall be disbursed as set forth in subsection (k) of Section 2-123 of this Code.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (625 ILCS 5/6-118 last amended P.A. 104-435, eff. 11-21-25)
new_rules.notes: Delegation followed for completeness: driver's-record abstracts are held by the Secretary of State; the figure binds that State office, not municipalities (applies_to state_agencies_only).

new_rules.legal_concept: Paper-copy fees inapplicable to records furnished electronically
new_rules.atomic_rule: Except to the extent the General Assembly expressly provides, statutory fees applicable to paper copies (including the 15-cent page fee) do not apply to records furnished in electronic format; only the recording-medium cost may be charged, so records delivered by e-mail or portal carry no copy fee.
new_rules.trigger: Records furnished to the requester in electronic format
new_rules.source_language: Except to the extent that the General Assembly expressly provides, statutory fees applicable to copies of public records when furnished in a paper format shall not be applicable to those records when furnished in an electronic format. A public body may charge the requester for the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (5 ILCS 140/6 last amended by P.A. 98-1129, eff. 12-3-14; no 2024-2026 amendment; verified against ILGA full-Act text on 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: PAC binding opinion 25-015 (Dec. 23, 2025): a body that maintains records only on paper may charge 15 cents/page for the paper copies even if it chooses to e-mail some of them, but a body that creates electronic copies is limited to the electronic-record fees. Confirms 'delivery: email' = no charge.

applicability_notes: 5 ILCS 140/2(a) defines 'public body' to include 'counties, townships, cities, villages, incorporated towns, school districts and all other municipal corporations' as well as State bodies; every Sec. 6 fee figure therefore binds municipalities directly with no separate agency schedule. Illinois has no 'uniform fee schedule' for State agencies that differs from the municipal regime for FOIA copies (State agencies are 'public bodies' under the same Sec. 6).
Sec. 6(e) (driver's-record abstracts → 625 ILCS 5/6-118, $20) binds the Secretary of State only; recorded as IL-9012 with applies_to state_agencies_only, not used to resolve any municipal item.

625 ILCS 5/11-416 crash-report fee (≤ $5 / ≤ $20) is a record-specific statutory fee that municipal police departments may charge in place of the Sec. 6(b) copy fee ('Except when a fee is otherwise fixed by statute'); it binds 'law enforcement agencies of local authorities'.

50 ILCS 345 (card acceptance) applies to 'units of local government' — municipalities — and is not part of FOIA; State agencies' payment methods are governed elsewhere. Recorded with medium confidence because it is a general statute.

Commercial-purpose (Sec. 6(f)), voluminous (Sec. 6(a-5), 3.6) and recurrent-requester (Sec. 3.2) fee/payment rules apply to all public bodies including municipalities but only to those request classes; several items (labor rates, prepayment, nonpayment) resolve as not_applicable/silent for ordinary municipal requests and are noted for the special classes.

The AG's guidance documents (FAQ 10/2023, webinar 4/10/2025, PAC Update Winter 2026) restate the statute and add no figures; the one guidance-vs-statute tension is the FAQ's 'may, but are not required to' description of the Sec. 6(c) waiver versus the statute's 'shall be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge, as determined by the public body'.
material_negatives: No labor rate for search, review/redaction or programming outside commercial requests (statutory prohibition, 6(a)/(b)); no overhead/fringe multiplier; no billing increment.

No per-requester periodic free-time allowance; no dollar deposit threshold; no deposit-percentage cap other than the 'pay in full' permission for the three special classes; no prepayment provision for ordinary requests.

No estimate threshold by amount, no requester response window to an estimate, no revised-estimate percentage, no estimate validity period, no clock effect for unpaid deposits, no overrun/re-issue rule.
No dollar de-minimis, no minimum fee, no request-level dollar maximum (actual cost is the cap), no postage/mailing/handling provision.
No per-recording or per-minute audio/video fee; electronic records limited to medium cost (PAC 25-014).
No percentage commercial surcharge; no fee carry-forward across repeat requests.

The Attorney General has promulgated no administrative rule setting FOIA fees for public bodies; the only fee instruments are the statute, the public body's own published scale, and PAC opinions interpreting Sec. 6.
gaps_manual_verification: rules.deposit.threshold / payment.productionGate: whether a public body may require payment before releasing copies on an ORDINARY (non-commercial, non-recurrent, non-voluminous) request is unaddressed in statute and in the AG guidance opened; a PAC determination or city-counsel call is needed.

labor.search.rate (voluminous carve-out): Sec. 6(a) exempts voluminous requests from its personnel-cost prohibition, but Sec. 6(b) and the AG FAQ treat search/review fees as commercial-only; confirm no hourly labor is chargeable on voluminous paper requests.
media/av: whether the recording-medium cost may be charged in addition to a 6(a-5) voluminous megabyte tier is not stated.
delivery: postage for mailed paper copies — statute and AG materials silent; treat as manual verification before a city charges actual postage.

waiver: whether refusal of a 6(c) waiver is a 'denial' reviewable by the PAC (6(d) names only 6(a)/(b)); FAQ describes waiver as discretionary while statute says 'shall ... as determined by the public body'.
rules.freePages unit: 'first 50 pages ... requested by a requester' — per request in practice (PAC 25-015), statute does not say per period.

PAC binding opinion 25-015 (Dec. 23, 2025) was read only through the AG's PAC Update Winter 2026 summary (the opinion PDF was not opened); its holding on paper-vs-electronic maintenance is noted, not quoted.
Sage Information Services v. Humm (2012 IL App (5th) 110580) and v. Suhr (2014 IL App (2d) 130708) are cited as quoted inside PAC 25-014; the opinions themselves were not opened (case-law boundary).

proposed_concept_keys.definition: A fee imposed inconsistently with the statutory fee limits is treated as a denial of access (opening the appeal/review path).
